agency_full: European Space Agency (Huygens probe, carried to Saturn by NASA/ASI Cassini orbiter)
payload: 318 kg ESA entry probe — aeroshell, 3 parachutes, 6 science packages (HASI, GCMS, DISR, ACP, SSP, DWE). Designed to survive 2.5-hour atmospheric descent through Titan's nitrogen–methane atmosphere to the surface.
delta_v: ~6 km/s (entry deceleration from 6 km/s hypersonic to surface)
credit: © ESA / NASA / JPL-Caltech / University of Arizona — Huygens probe data public domain. The Huygens probe rode aboard NASA's Cassini spacecraft on the 7-year VVEJGA interplanetary cruise to the Saturn system. Released 2004-12-25, it coasted 20 days before entering Titan's atmosphere on 2005-01-14. A heat shield slowed it from 6 km/s to subsonic, then three parachute stages (main chute at 160 km, drogue at 120 km, stabiliser for the final descent) let it drift for 2 hours 27 minutes through the haze, transmitting 350 images and full atmospheric profiles before touching down on a floodplain of rounded water-ice pebbles and a thin veneer of liquid methane. The landing site (10.3°S, 192.3°W) lies in a dark lowland drained by methane rivers from brighter highlands. Huygens returned data from the surface for ~72 minutes until Cassini set below its radio horizon. First and only soft landing in the outer solar system.

events.label: Launch (with Cassini)
events.description: Titan IVB / Centaur lifts the 5712 kg Cassini–Huygens stack from Cape Canaveral. Huygens rides aboard Cassini as an attached entry probe; the 7-year VVEJGA cruise to Saturn begins.

events.label: Venus #1 — gravity assist
events.description: First Venus flyby (1998-04-26, 284 km altitude). Gravity assist raises the spacecraft's aphelion as part of the energy-building VVEJGA sequence.

events.label: Venus #2 — gravity assist
events.description: Second Venus flyby (1999-06-24, 600 km). Together with the first assist, sets up the Earth flyby 55 days later.

events.label: Earth — gravity assist
events.description: 1171 km above the South Pacific (1999-08-18). The orbit is now energetic enough to cross Jupiter's.

events.label: Jupiter — gravity assist
events.description: 9.7 million km from Jupiter (2000-12-30). Final assist delivers the remaining velocity for Saturn arrival.

events.label: Saturn orbit insertion (Cassini)
events.description: Cassini's main-engine burn (2004-07-01) captures the stack into Saturn orbit. Huygens remains dormant, attached to Cassini, for the next six months while the orbiter homes in on a Titan flyby geometry.

events.label: Huygens release
events.description: Huygens released from Cassini on 2004-12-25, coasting toward Titan on a ballistic trajectory with no propulsion. The probe then hibernated for 20 days.

events.label: Titan atmosphere entry — EDL
events.description: 2005-01-14: entry at 6 km/s, heat shield slows to subsonic; main chute at 160 km deploys; 2.5-hour parachute descent through Titan's haze transmitting 350 images and full atmospheric profiles. Touchdown on a floodplain of rounded water-ice pebbles at 10.3°S, 192.3°W — the first and only soft landing in the outer solar system.
